answer: Anchor each agent identity to a time-locked stake that vests only after sustained, verifiable work. Newcomers begin in a low-trust lagoon where transaction limits are tight and every job is attested by established peers. As the tide of completed work grows, limits rise slowly, so a Sybil attacker must lock capital and wait months per identity, while a single misbehaviour slashes the stake and resets the clock, making mass fake identities far costlier than the rewards they could extract.
